cards.title: ASX 200 climbs as miners and property lead
cards.dek: The ASX 200 gained 0.6% to 8,735.7, with materials and real estate among the strongest sectors.
cards.insight: The interesting signal is the breadth: the rally is being driven by rate-sensitive property and resource stocks rather than just one narrow theme.

cards.title: Nasdaq hits a fresh record as AI stocks surge
cards.dek: US technology shares pushed the Nasdaq to another record, with Nvidia and Microsoft among the major drivers.
cards.insight: US equities are showing an unusual combination: long-term yields are elevated, yet earnings and AI expectations are still overpowering the valuation pressure.

cards.title: Bond yields remain the market's big risk
cards.dek: The US 10-year Treasury yield remains around 5.3%, while Australia's 10-year yield is around 5.4%.
cards.insight: If yields stay elevated, the next test for equities is whether earnings growth can keep pace with the higher discount rate.

cards.title: Oil pulls back below US$100
cards.dek: Brent crude slipped back below US$100 as supply concerns eased, helping risk sentiment across global markets.
cards.insight: For Australia, a softer oil price can take some pressure off inflation expectations while still leaving energy producers supported by historically high prices.

cards.title: Rio Tinto gains after asset monetisation signal
cards.dek: Rio Tinto rose after Morgan Stanley highlighted progress on potential asset monetisation in its Pilbara and Canadian infrastructure holdings.
cards.insight: Asset monetisation can matter beyond the headline: it may improve balance-sheet flexibility and create capital for higher-return projects or shareholder returns.

cards.title: Firmus launches a potential A$7bn IPO
cards.dek: Australian data-centre operator Firmus is moving ahead with an IPO that could raise about A$7 billion.
cards.insight: The deal is another sign that investors are willing to fund the infrastructure behind AI and digital growth — even while bond yields remain high.

cards.title: Australian consumer confidence slumps after rate hike
cards.dek: Consumer sentiment fell sharply after the RBA's latest rate increase, with Westpac flagging another possible hike in November.
cards.insight: This is the domestic counterweight to the strong US equity story: higher rates can support banks but increasingly pressure household spending and cyclicals.

cards.title: ASX vs US: two very different market engines
cards.dek: The US rally is being powered by AI and earnings optimism, while Australia's market is more exposed to rates, banks, property and commodities.
cards.insight: The big question for investors is whether Australia's resource and financial exposure can close the performance gap while US AI leadership remains intact.
